structured.approach: I read feat.tasks to find the Data Engineering tasks: TSK-01 and TSK-02, both in ap_pipeline. For each one I checked whether it needs any external access. Then I read every ap_pipeline file a secret could come from: CLAUDE.md, ci.py, and all source modules (__init__.py, ingest.py, transform.py, dq.py, pipeline.py, schedule.json). I also searched the checkout for credential patterns and found none. I compared what the tasks need with the permission-table tool view, which says nothing is required or granted. Since nothing is needed, there is no gap and no access request. I used no connector, because the inputs and the code answered the question. The scheduling runtime is not covered by the inputs, so I raised it as a non-blocking open question. Every claim cites only files I read in this session.

claims.text: The Data Engineering tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-02 is a pure function with no I/O, and TSK-01 builds on synthetic feed v3 rows. Feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates release, not coding.
The pipeline entry point run(csv_text) takes the feed as text and opens no connection.
Ingestion uses the standard library csv module to parse CSV text held in memory.
The transform and data-quality modules work on in-memory rows only and import only datetime, decimal and typing.
The ap_pipeline package version is 0.4.0, and TSK-01 owns the version step.

CI runs locally as /usr/bin/python3 ci.py. It compiles the code, runs the unit tests, measures coverage against a minimum of 90.0 and runs static checks, and it reads no environment variable or credential.
schedule.json defines a daily run at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata and references no credential.
No secrets are required or granted for ap_pipeline. Required and granted match (both none), so no access request is needed and there is no excess access.
ingest.py, pipeline.py and schedule.json are on TSK-01's must-not-change list, and a transport layer would re-trigger DES-01.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): schedule.json defines a daily run, but the inputs do not say which runtime executes the schedule or whether that runtime needs its own credential for the production feed. This should be re-checked at DE-13; it does not affect TSK-01 or TSK-02.
structured.summary: I rewrote task.secrets_scope.md for FEAT-ZD-48600 in full. The two Data Engineering tasks, TSK-01 (paid_date in the transform) and TSK-02 (the delays_by_vendor function), are pure-Python changes to ap_pipeline tested on synthetic data. They need no secrets in any environment. I read all the source files, ci.py and CLAUDE.md, and none of them uses an environment variable, credential or network connection. The permission-table tool view grants nothing, so required and granted match, there is no gap, and no access request was raised. There is one non-blocking question about credentials for the schedule runtime at DE-13. There are no blocking questions.
